# Pinned owned Chorala widget

This is the MIT-licensed **widget package**, not Chorala's AGPL server. Only the
standalone browser artifact is copied; the widget depends on bundled Preact
10.29.2 and does not import server packages. Both complete MIT notices remain in
this directory and in the served asset. `NOTICE` records the exact owned source
revision, build tools, lockfile hash and byte-for-byte artifact hash.

`source-widget.js` is the unchanged reviewed `@chorala/widget` artifact from
`webiumsk/chorala` revision `eec30fddde5d1d32da9e6848ff2cef32ba4ebe7a`
(runtime source `eec30fddde5d1d32da9e6848ff2cef32ba4ebe7a`). Do not edit it.
It replaces the older public distribution whose exact producing revision was
unknown; that historical source remains available in Git history.

`widget.js` is generated by `scripts/build-chorala-widget.mjs` and committed so
source imports and tests work before a production build. The generator verifies
the exact source hash, embedded licenses and JavaScript syntax, prepends the
provenance notice and removes only the footer for the undistributed source map.
It applies no minified-code patches. Vite imports the result with `?url`, producing
a content-hashed same-origin asset.

```sh
npm run build:chorala-widget
node scripts/build-chorala-widget.mjs --check
```

Generation uses no network or new dependency. Update the source revision, locked
build, licenses, hash and regression evidence together; no Satflux build silently
downloads or rebuilds the dependency. The source artifact was built with Node
24.22.1 and the owned fork's frozen pnpm 10.33.0 lock using the widget package's
`pnpm --filter @chorala/widget build` command. Hash equality is checked against the
reviewed artifact rather than assumed for arbitrary toolchain rebuilds.

The owned MIT package implements `refreshIdentity`, preserving the existing API
client, mounted UI, draft and screenshots when the JWT changes. Ordinary `identify`
and project changes clear account-bound state, including inline instances. Clearing
a JWT with `refreshIdentity({})` removes the header without retaining an expired
identity after SSO has explicitly been disabled.

Feedback diagnostic URL and referrer values contain HTTP origins only, excluding
paths, user information, query parameters and fragments. Screenshot capture remains
user initiated and reviewable. The widget includes EN/SK/ES/DE/CS plus inherited FR.

Changelog bodies render a safe Markdown subset: paragraphs, headings, lists,
emphasis, labelled web links, quotes and code. The renderer belongs to the MIT
widget package; no AGPL dashboard code is embedded. HTML and images remain inert
text. Existing changelog data does not require an import or migration. This asset
must be included in a new Satflux frontend build; upgrading the feedback server
alone does not update the widget embedded in Satflux.

The client still calls the configured Chorala API directly. Exact application
origins must be allowed in the project; pinning the script does not remove CORS
requirements. Satflux CSRF headers are never sent to Chorala. The proxy endpoint
remains protected by CSRF. Changing the server origin remains a protected operator
setting; this artifact update does not deploy or switch the service.
